<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **130** documentable anchor(s).

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 46 pages)`, `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3976902a6a6d887977c3b0ec390932927a9c1a86` — the merge of head `b3291114e08643d73f00d94f1b5a30b347ae20cb` into base `5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3976902a6a6d887977c3b0ec390932927a9c1a86 && git checkout 3976902a6a6d887977c3b0ec390932927a9c1a86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1 b3291114e08643d73f00d94f1b5a30b347ae20cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1 && git merge --no-ff b3291114e08643d73f00d94f1b5a30b347ae20cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b3291114e08643d73f00d94f1b5a30b347ae20cb`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds against the diff. `sys_sso_provider` gains one boolean column, `sign_out_of_idp`, default `false` with `trackHistory`. The vendor provider record gains the matching additional field. Edit Sign-In Options gains a param, and Register SAML Provider and Edit SAML Settings gain an optional `logoutUrl`, stored as the provider's single logout service with no new column. Every existing provider reads `false`, so sign-out and the two SAML logout endpoints answer as before; nothing served before is refused.
- The ruling (6866334319, item 4 → A) is met arm by arm. The switch is per provider, off by default, and audited. With it on, SAML signs out through single logout and OIDC through an RP-initiated redirect that carries `id_token_hint`. Incoming logout messages are accepted only when signed: both signature flags are forced on with the switch, and the ablation turns the two unsigned pins red. Saving the switch on for a provider that cannot honour it answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp`. With the switch off, the provider's incoming logout endpoint stays closed (pinned).
- The OIDC `post_logout_redirect_uri` is set only for a trusted origin, and the `end_session_endpoint` is accepted only on a trusted origin at save time. When the provider row or its options cannot be read, the scope falls back to switch off.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` holds: one new field on a platform object plus additive action params.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`, as the changeset declares: additive surface only, with nothing removed or narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` change and no governed path (`check-governed-merges --pr 33170`: not governed).
- The vendor (`@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12) is not patched. Its single-logout options are answered per request from the provider's scope.
- The generated translation bundles move with the new column and params, and no hand-written locale string is added.
- Remainders named in the PR, outside this review: the Console sign-out following the answered `url`, and any form item the form does not render by itself (the ui card). Sessions that started before the switch was turned on sign out of the platform only.
- Nits, with no effect on correctness or the contract: `samlLogoutServiceOf` accepts an `http:` IdP logout address, matching the other SAML address fields; the 7-day expiry fallback for a recorded OIDC session is an unnamed constant.

Implemented-by: `session_01L9qibz44EJYWFvzJTmGHkg`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibwMmGJKaQ52CgHqNu2`

**VERDICT: PASS**
